entries.spoken: So the plan for the authentication refactor is this. First, we move the token validation out of the Express middleware and into a dedicated service. The refresh token expires after one day, and we store the session in Redis so the API response can be cached. Then we add a PostgreSQL index on the email column, run npm install, and then npm run dev to make sure everything still works locally before opening the pull request.
entries.reference: So the plan for the authentication refactor is this. First, we move the token validation out of the Express middleware and into a dedicated service. The refresh token expires after one day, and we store the session in Redis so the API response can be cached. Then we add a PostgreSQL index on the email column, run npm install, and then npm run dev to make sure everything still works locally before opening the pull request.

entries.spoken: Okay, so I looked into the bug with the checkout page. It turns out handle submit is being called twice because the use effect hook doesn't have a dependency array. I think the fix is to move the API call into a separate function, maybe call it create order, and make sure is loading is set before the request goes out.
entries.reference: Okay, so I looked into the bug with the checkout page. It turns out handleSubmit is being called twice because the useEffect hook doesn't have a dependency array. I think the fix is to move the API call into a separate function, maybe call it createOrder, and make sure isLoading is set before the request goes out.

entries.spoken: For the deployment, let's keep it simple. We build the Docker image in GitHub Actions, push it to the registry, and then the Kubernetes deployment pulls the new tag. If the pods fail the health check, we roll back to the previous version. We don't need Helm for now.
